#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the
# backup destination.
#
# Destination is not hard-coded here (it wasn't decided at the time this was
# written). Configure it via the BACKUP_DEST environment variable, e.g. in
# the crontab/job definition:
#
#   BACKUP_DEST=backup-host:/srv/backups ./backup.sh
#   BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups ./backup.sh
#
# If BACKUP_DEST is not set, the tarball is copied to ./backups so the job
# still succeeds and produces a usable artifact; update BACKUP_DEST (or the
# default below) once the real destination is decided.
set -eu

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-logs}"
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-./backups}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" "$LOG_DIR/"

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # host:path form -> copy over the network
        scp -q "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # local path or mount point
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"
